takeaways.label: All cylinders firing, broad-based strength
takeaways.text: Every business vertical delivered strong performance, with HPP, Specialty and CDMO all posting sequential growth driven by volumes, pricing and operational efficiency.

takeaways.label: HFO contract extended, base protected
takeaways.text: The Solstice supply contract was extended 4 years to December 2032, turning a 7-year deal into an 11-year deal with larger volumes on the same asset base, providing visibility beyond FY28.

takeaways.label: CDMO pipeline is breaking through
takeaways.text: One molecule won China approval with US FDA fast-track, another targets darolutamide label expansion; management says a revenue trajectory into the ₹1,200–1,300 crore range is "not sort of unimaginable" beyond FY27.

takeaways.label: Margins held despite cost headwinds
takeaways.text: Forex tailwinds and pricing actions largely offset sourcing cost increases, while operating leverage and efficiency efforts protected EBITDA; management is working towards full-year margins in the same range as H1.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: R32 plant commissioning and ramp, Chemours project commissioning in Q3, and whether the debottlenecking recently commissioned at Dahej starts feeding into Specialty numbers.

sections.title: HFO Contract Extension & the Solstice Business

points.label: Contract now 11 years
points.text: The existing supply contract with Solstice Advanced Materials was extended by 4 years, taking it from a 7-year to an 11-year contract through December 2032.

points.label: Larger volumes, same assets
points.text: The extension is not just a time extension; management expects volumes to be larger on the same asset base, meaning revenue and period both expand without incremental capex.

points.label: Base protected through FY30
points.text: The extension provides visibility beyond FY28, with the base protected through FY30.

points.label: Pricing mechanism is pass-through
points.text: When pressed on whether the implied annual run rate moderates beyond FY29, management declined to confirm simplistic math, citing complex commercial structures and pass-through pricing where capex recovery changes the rate.

points.label: Own HFO commercialization not in conflict
points.text: Management stated own HFO commercialization will not conflict with the Solstice contract because there are 40+ varieties of HFOs serving different applications; the company is exploring both partnership and product models.

points.label: HFO is a premium product
points.text: HFO serves greener, cleaner end applications and commands a premium; global HFO capacity is only 10% of global ref gas demand in tonnage terms, so there is not enough volume to play on pricing alone.

quotes.text: Ganatra: "The way to look at this is that on a same asset base, you're going to extend both the volumes, the revenues and also the period. This was a 7-year contract. This now becomes an 11-year contract."

sections.title: CDMO: Pipeline Breakthroughs and Capacity Build

points.label: Two molecules advancing fast
points.text: One molecule has already received approval in China and is on fast track for FDA approval in the US market; the other relates to potential label expansion of darolutamide, an existing commercial molecule.

points.label: USD 10 crore target within reach
points.text: Management says the CDMO business is at striking distance of the USD 10 crore run rate target in terms of order book visibility, with growth expected by end of this year.

points.label: Beyond FY27, the numbers get large
points.text: cGMP-4 Phase 1+2 carries peak annual revenue potential of ~₹900–1,000 crores by FY28/FY29; management said envisaging growth into the ₹1,200–1,300 crore range is "not sort of unimaginable" given the label expansion and China approval developments.

points.label: cGMP-5 trigger is clear
points.text: Phase 5 will be triggered when GMP plant utilization reaches 70–80%, with "absolutely no doubt"; infrastructure (warehouse up to Phase 6, ETP up to Phase 5) is already in place, enabling a quick move.

points.label: cGMP-4 Phase 2 on track
points.text: Expected to become operational by end of Q4 FY27.

points.label: European CDMO engagement deepening
points.text: Engagement with a leading European CDMO major is deepening, driven by increasing demand for an existing molecule and an expanding role in the customer's supply chain.

points.label: Balanced portfolio build
points.text: The strategic focus is a balanced portfolio of late-stage and commercial molecules complemented by early-stage programs, expanding across oncology, cardiovascular, neurology and animal health.

quotes.text: Ganatra: "Envisaging a growth beyond FY27 in the numbers that you talked about is not sort of unimaginable."

sections.title: Specialty Chemicals: Extracting More from Existing Assets

points.label: Strong order visibility
points.text: The Specialty Chemicals business has strong order visibility for H2 FY27 and beyond, with a product pipeline expanding across existing and new molecules.

points.label: Growth from operational efficiency, not new capex
points.text: Sequential growth was driven by extracting more from current assets: more campaigns in the same plants through product mapping and step minimization, supported by R&D and innovation.

points.label: Five new molecules contributing
points.text: Part of the growth seen in the quarter came from 5 new molecules being worked on; campaign orders for those molecules extend through the end of this year and beyond.

points.label: MPP-1 and MPP-2 exceeding PAR
points.text: By the end of FY27, the PAR of MPP-1 and MPP-2 will have been "far exceeded" due to work mapping more products into those plants and debottlenecking.

points.label: Debottlenecking not yet in numbers
points.text: The recently commissioned debottlenecking of MPP capacity at Dahej (September 2026) is not yet factored into reported numbers and should drive growth beyond current levels.

points.label: ₹350 crore run rate going higher
points.text: Management confirmed the Specialty chemicals run rate will go up from current levels due to the factors above.

points.label: Agri-specialty approach is asset-light
points.text: The approach is to utilize current assets and extract more from them rather than build new dedicated capacity.

sections.title: HPP: Pricing, Volumes and the Ref Gas Advantage

points.label: Revenue growth from volumes and realization
points.text: HPP revenue growth was driven by higher volumes and improved realization, with the pricing environment for HFC remaining firm and realization improving sequentially.

points.label: AHF plant utilization improved
points.text: AHF plant utilization improvement contributed to growth momentum, though the plant is not yet at full capacity given its large size.

points.label: AHF merchant sales larger than planned
points.text: Merchant sales volumes are far larger than originally planned; some material was placed in international markets and is also serving high-purity HF.

points.label: Ref gas pricing beats averages
points.text: Management emphasized that teams placed product at better pricing than averages suggest, calling reliance on averages a "danger" that understates the upside captured.

points.label: HFO business contributed sequentially
points.text: QoQ growth in the Orchid/Solstice HFO business contributed to sequential growth.

points.label: R32 plant commissioning shortly
points.text: The R32 plant will commission shortly and ramp up towards the end of Q3 FY27, with full ramp-up possibly in Q4 FY27.

points.label: HFC capacity expansion on track
points.text: Progressing as planned, remains on track for commissioning "shortly."

quotes.text: Ganatra: "This is the danger of relying on averages, right? I mean averages don't tell you what we kind of -- our teams managed to place the product at better pricing."

sections.title: New Engines: Chemours, Advanced Materials, TDF

points.label: Chemours commissioning in Q3 FY27
points.text: The project is progressing towards commissioning in Q3 FY27; the delay was a "conscious choice" between partners, evidenced by purchase orders already in hand as the asset nears commissioning.

points.label: Chemours product qualified for hypercomputing
points.text: Earlier in the year, Chemours qualified its product with French company 2CRSi (an OEM manufacturer of high-compute kits) via a joint development agreement, accelerating adoption in hypercomputing.

points.label: Scale-up timeline is 15 months post-commissioning
points.text: Management said it will take about 15 months once the project is commissioned to know adoption rate, market size, and hence final capex; premature to talk about eventual capex.

points.label: Advanced Materials as a new vertical
points.text: The company is incubating Advanced Materials as a new business vertical, focusing on specialized applications across data centers, electronics, semiconductors and defense; expected to be ~10–15% of the expanded pie by 2030 and positioned as a growth business for the next decade.

points.label: Advanced Materials capacity by Q2 FY28
points.text: Adoption capacity is progressing as per schedule, expected to commission by Q2 FY28.

points.label: TDF project with DRDO progressing well
points.text: The project is on schedule; management noted that as the product is developed, the pharma application will be accelerated sooner than the defense timeline since defense qualification takes longer.

quotes.text: Ganatra: "In fact, the delay is a conscious choice rather than anything else between the partners. And this is evidenced by the fact that as we are coming to commission that asset, we already have orders in place coming in for the future quarters."

sections.title: Margins, Capex and the Cost Equation

points.label: EBITDA protected on multiple fronts
points.text: Forex tailwind and pricing actions largely offset sourcing cost impacts; operating leverage and operating efficiency efforts also helped protect EBITDA.

points.label: 34% HF EBITDA from efficiency, not just pricing
points.text: Management attributed the 34% EBITDA in the current environment not only to pricing but continuously to efficiencies and improvements, even as raw material costs (sulfur, gas, fluorspar) rise.

points.label: FY27 full-year margins in H1 range
points.text: The company is working towards margins in the same sort of range as H1.

points.label: Long-term 30% EBITDA guidance unchanged
points.text: Management maintained the 30% long-term EBITDA margin guidance but cautioned against predicting 5–6 year margins given geopolitical volatility.

points.label: Capex frame ₹700–1,000 crores annually
points.text: FY27 is at the lower end (~₹700 crores); growth to FY28 is "pretty much baked in" with capexes in place, with some part going to FY29 (e.g., cGMP-4). Several projects are in the hopper and will be announced as they mature through stage gates.

points.label: Renewable energy investment
points.text: The company is investing to meet more than 60% of energy requirements through renewable resources.

points.label: Nectar ramp on track
points.text: FY27 utilization expected at 60–65% of PAR, with balance PAR in FY28.

quotes.text: Ganatra: "I will not sit here and let you believe that I have full knowledge of the future. In fact, if at all, our cognitive ability does not allow us to predict the numbers for 5 years and 6 years on EBITDA margins. The geopolitics are massively volatile, as you all know."

items.title: Group growth target to 2030
items.text: Management targets 20-25% overall revenue growth to 2030, with advanced materials expected to contribute 10-15% of the expanded revenue pie by then. Against FY26 revenue of ₹4,066 cr growing 45.68%, that implies the company is compounding from a base already running at ~34% EBITDA margins.

items.title: R32 capacity expansion
items.text: The ₹236.5 cr, 15,000 MTPA R32 plant is commissioning in Q3 FY27 with full ramp-up expected the following quarter, on top of current 9,000-10,000 tonnes capacity. Peak revenue potential is ₹600-825 cr per annum, and customers are signing five-year contracts covering a targeted 35-45% of capacity.

items.title: CDMO cGMP4 Phase 2
items.text: Phase 2 of the cGMP-4 plant (₹125 cr, fully dedicated to the European partner Fermion) is expected operational by end of Q4 FY27, with Phases 1 and 2 together carrying peak revenue potential of ₹900-1,000 cr by FY28-29. Management reaffirmed the ₹1,000 cr CDMO revenue target for FY27, with segment revenue already up 78% YoY in Q2 FY27.

items.title: Chemours liquid cooling plant
items.text: The Opteon two-phase immersion cooling plant (₹120 cr capex, 35% funded by Chemours) is commissioning in Q3 FY27 with purchase orders in place for Q4 FY27 deliveries; Navin is the sole manufacturer of this fluid globally. A ~10x scale-up capex decision is expected within ~15 months of commissioning against a global liquid cooling market management sizes near $3 billion.

items.title: Solstice HFO contract extension
items.text: The HFO supply contract with Solstice Advanced Materials was extended by four years to December 2032, adding ~US$180 mn of revenue potential and taking total contract value to ~$590 mn over 11 years. Volumes under the extension are expected to be larger than before with pass-through pricing, protecting the revenue base beyond FY28-29.

items.title: Dahej MPP debottlenecking
items.text: The ₹75 cr debottlenecked MPP capacity at Dahej was commissioned on 29 Sep 2026, serving a purchase order from a global crop-protection innovator for CY26. Peak revenue potential is ₹140-160 cr per annum at a 2x asset turn, and this growth is not yet in reported numbers.

items.title: Advanced materials adoption capex
items.text: The ₹90 cr adoption-capacity build at Surat for data-centre, electronics, semiconductor and defence applications is on schedule, with the first phase complete around end-Q4 FY27 and full completion by Q2 FY28. Four to five products are already customer-approved at lab scale, and the DRDO sodium borohydride TDF project targets a pharma market of roughly ₹400 cr in India.

items.title: Dahej AHF plant ramp
items.text: The 40,000 TPA anhydrous HF plant at Dahej (₹450 cr) commenced commercial production on 6 Feb 2026, with its revenues kicking into FY28 as it ramps toward full capacity. The capacity underpins the R32 expansion and merchant HF sales, and opens the path to high-purity and electronic-grade HF.
